answer: Most black holes start as very big stars, at least about 20 times heavier than the Sun. A star stays puffed up because of the energy from burning fuel in its middle, and that pushes out against its own weight. When the fuel runs out, the push stops, and the star falls in on itself very fast, often with a huge explosion called a supernova [1][2]. If what's left is heavy enough, more than about three Suns' worth, nothing can stop it from getting crushed smaller and smaller. In the end its pull is so strong that not even light can get out, and that's a black hole [1]. After that, black holes can get bigger by pulling in gas or by joining with other black holes [1].
